findings.finding: The rejection names no status code. The publish operation offers several error statuses, so a tester cannot write the assertion. The error text in the technical details covers only the overall score, not a failing dimension.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-27998/AC2: "an explicit error is returned explaining the reason (reached score value and threshold)"; technical details: "Error message: \"Quality Score X is below treshold Y.\""; catalogue-be POST /self-descriptions/resource responses 400, 409, 422.
findings.question: Which status code and which message does a quality rejection return, for an overall-score failure and for a dimension-score failure?
options: 422 Unprocessable Entity with the score and threshold in the problem detail
400 Bad Request with the same detail

findings.finding: AC2 says a rejected description is not stored; AC3 says only that it is not published. A builder can read AC3 either way. The technical error also has no status and "the failure reason is logged" has no observable oracle.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-27998/AC2: "the resource description is not stored"; SIMPL-27998/AC3: "the resource description is not published in the catalogue / an explicit technical error is returned / the failure reason is logged."
findings.question: On a technical failure of the quality assessment, is the description stored (unpublished) or not stored at all, and which status is returned?
options: not stored, 500 or 503 returned
stored as unpublished, error returned

findings.finding: The technical details list an invalid-QAR scenario and an endpoint-failure scenario that no criterion describes as an outcome; AC3 only gives a missing threshold as an example. It is also not said which metadata quality definition applies when several schemas have their own active profile.
findings.evidence: Technical details: "Cover pass, reject, invalid-QAR, endpoint-failure, and configuration-error scenarios"; SIMPL-27998/AC1: "the overall threshold defined in the metadata quality definition"; catalogue-client-be GET /schemas/{schemaName}/qualityProfiles/active (one profile per schema).
findings.question: Does an invalid QAR or an unreachable scoring endpoint fall under AC3, and is the threshold taken from the active profile of the description's schema?

findings.finding: The scale of the score is open. The quick-search API example uses a fraction (overallScore 0.92, minimumScore 0.8), the advanced-search example uses minimumScore 75, and the classification note uses percent ranges. A test with minimum score 75 passes under one reading and returns nothing under the other.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-29292/AC2, SIMPL-29293/AC2: "overallScore greater than or equal to the minimum score"; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /governanceAuthority/selfDescriptions example minimumScore 0.8, overallScore 0.92; POST /selfDescriptions/advancedSearch example minimumScore: 75; SIMPL-29292/AC3 note: "\"Sufficient\": 40-70 %".
findings.question: Is the score a fraction from 0 to 1 or a percentage from 0 to 100, and what is the upper bound the UI accepts?
options: 0 to 1

findings.finding: Classifications and their order come from "the active MQP", but a quick search has no schema, and each schema has its own active profile. The UI cannot know which list of classifications to offer, nor which ranges order them.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-29292/AC3 note: "defined and named by the Governance Authority as part of the active Metadata Quality Profile (MQP)"; catalogue-client-be GET /schemas/{schemaName}/qualityProfiles/active (per schema name).
findings.question: For quick search, which profile supplies the classification list and the ordering: one profile per data space, the profile of each result's schema, or a union?
options: one data-space-wide profile
per result, using the profile of its schema
union of all active profiles

findings.finding: Advanced search has a selected schema, so its active profile is the natural source of the classifications. The example ranges overlap at the bounds (40 in Poor and Sufficient), and the API examples use other labels (Green, good). The sensible default should be confirmed.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-29293/AC3 note: "Poor: 0-40 %", "Sufficient: 40-70 %"; t2-fc-openapi.yaml example overallClassification: Green; minimumClassification: good.
findings.question: Is the classification list taken from the active profile of the selected schema, and is a range bound inclusive at the lower end?

findings.finding: AC6 (description without a score while a filter is active) and AC7 (invalid filter input) are struck, but the API returns descriptions with overallScore null and defines 400 errors for invalid values, and the technical details still ask for inline validation. A builder has to guess both behaviours.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-29292 and SIMPL-29293: "-AC6- ... excluded from the filtered result set-", "-AC7- ... the UI shows a clear validation message-"; technical details: "Add input validation and inline error messages for invalid score/classification inputs"; t2-fc-openapi.yaml example overallScore: null.
findings.question: With a quality filter active, are descriptions without a score excluded, and how does the UI handle an invalid score or a negative value?
options: unscored descriptions are excluded, invalid input blocked in the UI
unscored descriptions are kept, the API 400 is shown

findings.finding: The advanced-search story says "Quick Search behavior remains unchanged", a copy from the quick-search twin.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-29293/AC5: "Then Quick Search behavior remains unchanged and quality filters are not applied."
findings.question: Confirm that AC5 means Advanced Search behaviour.

findings.finding: The note says the story is implemented by the authentication provider, a component outside this input set, and that the story exists only for linkage. Its Then also asks to let the Consumer choose the catalogue, which SIMPL-31102 and SIMPL-31103 cover.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-30848 note: "This US is covered with the implementation of [...]authentication-provider-be[...] and only for linkage to the epic."; SIMPL-30848/AC1: "enable the Consumer to choose the catalogue of the Trustor Governance Authority".
findings.question: Is anything in SIMPL-30848 built or tested in the catalogue component, or is it out of scope here?

findings.finding: The role is left blank and "endpoint details" are not named. A note gives a URL rule (base URL plus a catalogue suffix), but the AC does not say what is provided or what is checked. No negative case (invalid endpoint, missing role) exists.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-30848/AC1: "with a role authorising __ federated search configuration", "When I provide the endpoint details of a Trustor Governance Authority"; note: "the catalogue url is <base-url> + \"catalogue-suffix\"".
findings.question: Which role, which fields make up the endpoint configuration, and what happens on an invalid or unreachable endpoint?

findings.finding: The criteria require POST /schemas/{schemaName}/versions with multipart form data and a 201. No entry OpenAPI file has this operation, so the request fields, the response body and the error statuses are undefined.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-30850/AC1 to AC3: "send a POST request to the /schemas/{schemaName}/versions endpoint with the form data as multipart/form-data"; SIMPL-31817/AC1: "POST /schemas/<schemaName>/versions"; inventory-review: "no /schemas/{schemaName}/versions operation exists in the entry files".
findings.question: Where is the versioning operation defined (which component, which contract), and which fields does it take?

findings.finding: AC1 says schemaType may be left empty and defaults to RESOURCE; AC2 lists schemaType as a required field; AC4 names only the changelog and the file as validated fields. The UI cannot both require the field and default it.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-30850/AC1: "I fill in changelog message but do not fill schemaType" ... "schemaType was set to \"RESOURCE\" as default value"; SIMPL-30850/AC2: "all required fields in the form, i.e. a changelog message and schemaType field"; SIMPL-30850/AC4: "I leave the changelog blank, or do not upload a file".
findings.question: Is schemaType required on the Create New Version form, or optional with RESOURCE as default?
options: required, no default
optional, defaults to RESOURCE

findings.finding: Creating a new version of the one federated search schema is a main path, yet a 409 is required when "another federated search schema is already published". If the schema being versioned counts as already published, the main path can never succeed.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-30850/AC3: "viewing the details page for the federated search schema ... schemaType = SEARCH ... 201 Created"; SIMPL-30850/AC5: "409 Conflict (if another federated search schema is already published)"; SIMPL-31817/AC3: "there is already another published federated search schema ... 409".
findings.question: Does the 409 apply only when the published SEARCH schema has a different name than the one being versioned?
options: 409 only when a SEARCH schema with another name is published
409 whenever any SEARCH schema is published, versioning needs revocation first

findings.finding: No criterion covers a user without the schema-management role (button hidden, or 403 shown), and AC1 and AC2 give two different role descriptions for the same action.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-30850/AC1: "with a role authorising schema management"; SIMPL-30850/AC2: "a logged-in user with the governance-admin role".
findings.question: What does the UI do for a user without the role, and which role is meant?

findings.finding: The validation and error messages are described as clear and user-friendly without texts; one example is given. This leaves wording to the builder, which is fine if confirmed.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-30850/AC4: "clear, inline validation error messages"; SIMPL-30850/AC5: "a clear, user-friendly error message ... (e.g., \"The uploaded schema file is invalid\")".
findings.question: Are message texts free, or is there a list to follow?

findings.finding: AC3 combines a resourceType in the request (a 400 under AC2) with an existing published schema (a 409). The order of the checks is not stated, so a test of AC3 may get 400 instead of 409. The status is also written "409 Config" here and "409 Conflict" in SIMPL-31815/AC3.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31817/AC2: "And a resourceType for instance \"DATA\" is specified ... 400 Bad Request"; SIMPL-31817/AC3: "there is already another published federated search schema ... And a resourceType for instance \"DATA\" is specified ... (409 Config)".
findings.question: Is the resourceType clause in AC3 intended, and if so, which check wins: 400 or 409?
options: drop the resourceType clause from AC3
keep it, 409 takes precedence
keep it, 400 takes precedence

findings.finding: Invalid SHACL, a missing name or title, and a caller without GA_SCHEMA_ADMIN are left to tickets outside this input set, so a builder has no expected status for them.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31815 hints: "The other negative scenrios are in this ticket SIMPL-13353"; SIMPL-31817 technical details: "The other negative scenarios are in this ticket SIMPL-13357".
findings.question: Which statuses apply to an invalid definition, a missing field and a caller without the role?

findings.finding: The list of selectable catalogues comes from an API "implemented under ticket SIMPL-33471" that is in no entry file. The criteria cannot be built or tested against a defined response.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31102 and SIMPL-31103 technical details: "The API used to retrieve the list of trusted dataspaces is exposed by the xfsc-adv-search component through the API implemented under ticket SIMPL-33471"; catalogue-client-be v2 has no such operation.
findings.question: Which operation returns the selectable catalogues, and what is its response shape?

findings.finding: The selection list holds "the catalogues of all trustor authorities". SIMPL-31142 and SIMPL-35874 also talk about selecting the local catalogue. It is open whether own catalogues appear in the same selector.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31102/AC1: "select one or more catalogues from the catalogues of all trustor authorities"; SIMPL-35874/AC1: "only the local catalogue is selected"; SIMPL-31142 technical design: "create dedicated tabs for the local catalogue and each federated catalogue".
findings.question: Does the catalogue selector list own catalogues together with the Trustor catalogues?
options: one selector with own and Trustor catalogues
Trustor catalogues only; the local catalogue is always searched

findings.finding: The business process also allows a search in all federated catalogues without selecting them, while the federated search API requires a non-empty catalogue selection and no story offers "all".
findings.evidence: BP6.1.2: "Searching in all federated catalogues without explicitely selecting them"; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /governanceAuthority/selfDescriptions: catalogueIds required, minItems 1.
findings.question: Is "search all federated catalogues" in scope for this release?
options: out of scope for now
UI selects all by default

findings.finding: No criterion covers an empty catalogue list (no Trustor yet), and the error text is "appropriate". Both have an easy default, to be confirmed.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31102/AC2, SIMPL-31103/AC2: "an appropriate error message is displayed to the user."
findings.question: What does the selector show when there are no Trustor catalogues?

findings.finding: The Trustor-side search operation (receiving a forwarded quick or advanced search) is in no entry file; the adapter calls it "the separate SIMPL-31880 API". AC2 requires a 403 on an operation whose path, parameters, attribute header and response are undefined.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31138/AC2: "I reject the request with error code 403"; SIMPL-31138 technical design: "implement API Simpl-31875"; SIMPL-31139: "implement API Simpl-31877"; t1-adapter-openapi.yaml: "Quick-search delegation to Trustor Governance Authorities is defined separately in SIMPL-31880".
findings.question: Which contract defines the Trustor-side search operations, and can it be added to the input set?

findings.finding: The Trustor rejects a non-trusted caller with 403, while the Trusted side expects a failed mTLS handshake (502) for the same broken trust. A failed handshake never reaches HTTP, so a 403 can only happen for a caller with a valid certificate. The two tests need different set-ups.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31138/AC2, SIMPL-31139/AC2: "from someone who is not a Trusted GA ... reject the request with error code 403"; SIMPL-31113/AC2: "no longer consider trusted GA as trusted ... reject the call to this trustor GA with an error code 502 failed mTLS handshake".
findings.question: Which caller gets 403 at the Trustor (valid certificate but no federation?), and which case ends in a handshake failure?
options: 403 for an authenticated caller without federation; handshake failure for a revoked certificate
always handshake failure; drop the 403

findings.finding: No criterion covers a forwarded request without identity attributes, an attribute with no mapping, an unavailable mapping service, or an invalid request. SIMPL-31150 lists these cases for the detail request; the search side is silent.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31138/AC1: "the Consumer's identity attributes are mapped according to the federation-defined attribute mappings"; SIMPL-31114/AC1: "make the mapped attributes available"; SIMPL-31150 technical description: "the identity mapping is unavailable".
findings.question: What does the Trustor return when attributes are missing, unmapped, or the mapping service is down?

findings.finding: The story is linkage-only and its one criterion repeats SIMPL-31138/AC1 and SIMPL-31139/AC1 with less detail. It adds no requirement of its own.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31106 note: "covered with the implementation of SIMPL-33462 ... SIMPL-33465 ... and only for linkage to the epic"; SIMPL-31106/AC1: "replies to trusted governance authority with the resource descriptions matching the search criteria".
findings.question: Confirm that SIMPL-31106 adds nothing beyond SIMPL-31138 and SIMPL-31139.

findings.finding: "At least one of the search terms is found in at least one of its properties" needs a rule for splitting the search string into terms. The API takes one searchString that may contain spaces. Two readings give different results for "climate data".
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31111/AC1: "at least one of the search terms is found in at least one of its properties"; SIMPL-31138/AC1: "at least one of the properties match the search terms"; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /selfDescriptions: one searchString, pattern allows whitespace.
findings.question: Is the search string split on whitespace with OR between terms, or matched as one phrase? Is matching case-insensitive and by substring?
options: split on whitespace, any term matches (OR)
whole string as one phrase

findings.finding: "Each search term is found in the property to which it was submitted" does not say whether found means equal, contains, or a typed comparison (numbers, dates).
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31112/AC1: "each search term is found in the property to which it was submitted"; SIMPL-31139/AC1: "whose properties match the search terms for that property".
findings.question: Which comparison applies per property type in advanced search?

findings.finding: Local quick search must keep only descriptions from the catalogues in the query, but the local quick-search operations have no catalogue parameter (the local advanced search body does have catalogueIds).
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31111/AC1: "I select the resource descriptions belong to one of my catalogues specified in the search query"; SIMPL-31767/AC1: "from one of the selected catalogues in search request from my data space"; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /selfDescriptions and catalogue-be GET /selfDescriptions/quickSearch: no catalogue parameter.
findings.question: How does a local quick search carry the catalogue selection, or is the own data space always one catalogue?

findings.finding: The linkage-only stories for local search start from "the Consumer is authorised" and give no outcome for a Consumer without the search role or without a token. The ABAC roles in the API (CATALOGUE_SEARCHER and others) are not named.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31111/AC1, SIMPL-31112/AC1: "And the Consumer is authorised with the identity attributes for searching"; catalogue-be GET /selfDescriptions/quickSearch: "Required ABAC roles (any one of): CATALOGUE_SEARCHER, ...".
findings.question: What does a search return for a Consumer without a search role: 403, or an empty list filtered by policy?

findings.finding: For a Trustor that no longer trusts, SIMPL-31113 rejects the call with 502, while SIMPL-31140 and SIMPL-31142 return an empty group for that catalogue and leave the others unaffected. A builder cannot tell whether the Consumer gets 502 or 200 with an empty group.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31113/AC2: "Simpl-Open reject the call to this trustor GA with an error code 502 failed mTLS handshake"; SIMPL-31140/AC3: "a Trustor Governance Authority cannot authenticate the request ... Simpl-Open returns an empty group for that catalogue".
findings.question: Is the 502 internal (between the GAs, turned into an empty group for the Consumer) or the status the Consumer receives?
options: internal only; Consumer gets 200 with an empty group
Consumer gets 502 for the whole search

findings.finding: A catalogue that belongs to no federation has no Trustor to call, so no handshake can fail. A 400 for an unknown catalogue identifier is the other natural reading.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31113/AC3: "there is one federated catalogue selected which does not belong to a federation ... error code 502 failed mTLS handshake"; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /governanceAuthority/selfDescriptions defines 400 for invalid catalogue selection.
findings.question: For an unknown or unfederated catalogue identifier, is the result 502, 400, or an empty group?
options: 400 Bad Request
empty group, others unaffected

findings.finding: No criterion covers a Trustor that is unreachable or slow, and no timeout value is named, while SIMPL-31140/AC3 only covers "cannot authenticate, or returns no results".
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31113/AC1: "forward the search request to each relevant Trustor Governance Authority via API"; SIMPL-31140/AC3: "cannot authenticate the request, or returns no results".
findings.question: What happens when a Trustor does not answer, and after how long?

findings.finding: The criteria require results grouped per catalogue, each group naming its catalogue and GA, with independent paging. The federated search operation returns one flat items list with one page block and says it does not define aggregation.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31140/AC1: "the results remain grouped per catalogue, each group identifying its catalogue and the Governance Authority"; SIMPL-31140/AC2: "paging information for each catalogue group independently"; t1-adapter-openapi.yaml GET /governanceAuthority/selfDescriptions: searchResponsePayload {totalCount, items, page, pageSize, ...}, "does not define orchestration, result aggregation, or partial-failure rules".
findings.question: What is the grouped response shape, and how does a client ask for the next page of one group?

findings.finding: SIMPL-31140/AC1 returns own and federated results "in a single response", while the SIMPL-31142 technical design has the UI call the local search API and the federated search API separately and build the tabs itself. These are two different builds.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31140/AC1: "Simpl-Open returns the results to the initiating Consumer in a single response"; SIMPL-31142 technical design: "Local Search -> invoke the local catalogue search API ... Federated Search -> invoke the federated search API (SIMPL-33462)".
findings.question: Does the backend merge own and federated results into one response, or does the UI combine two calls?
options: backend returns one grouped response
UI makes two calls and groups the results

findings.finding: "Own catalogues (if relevant)" does not say when the own catalogue is searched in a federated search.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31140/AC1: "have obtained the results by performing the search on my own catalogues (if relevant)".
findings.question: Is the own catalogue searched only when the Consumer selected it?

findings.finding: An authentication failure and a genuine empty result both give an empty group, so the Consumer cannot tell them apart and a tester cannot tell a fault from no matches.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31140/AC3: "When a Trustor Governance Authority cannot authenticate the request, or returns no results / Then Simpl-Open returns an empty group for that catalogue".
findings.question: Should a failed group carry a status or error marker next to the empty list?

findings.finding: Federated groups must omit the quality score, but the federated search operation returns overallScore and overallClassification per item and accepts minimumScore and minimumClassification as filters. It is open whether the quality filter applies to federated catalogues.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31140/AC4: "it is omitted for groups from catalogues of a Trustor Governance Authority"; t1-adapter-openapi.yaml GET /governanceAuthority/selfDescriptions: parameters minimumScore, minimumClassification; example items overallScore: 0.92; BP6.7.2: main properties only.
findings.question: For federated catalogues, are the quality fields removed from the response, and is a quality filter ignored or applied by the Trustor?
options: fields removed, filter ignored for federated catalogues
fields removed, filter applied at the Trustor
fields kept

findings.finding: The four criteria of this UI story are copies of the backend criteria of SIMPL-31140, written from the GA's view. The UI behaviour (one tab per catalogue, navigation) is only in the technical design, so no criterion tests the UI.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31142/AC1: "When I, the Governance Authority, have obtained the results" (same text as SIMPL-31140/AC1); technical design: "The UI dynamically creates one tab for each federated catalogue selected in the search request."
findings.question: Should SIMPL-31142 get UI criteria for the tabs, with SIMPL-31140 owning the backend criteria?

findings.finding: "The main properties" is the pass condition for every overview, but no story or API lists them.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31141/AC1, SIMPL-31767/AC1, SIMPL-31768/AC1: "for each resource description in the list I receive the main properties"; SIMPL-31142 technical design: "according to the existing search results view".
findings.question: Which properties are the main properties (for example name, description, offering type, access point)?

findings.finding: The process requires the own-catalogue overview to show the overall quality score and classification and to be sortable on main and quality properties. The overview criteria mention neither.
findings.evidence: BP6.7.1: "Overall metadata quality score and quality classification. This list can be sorted based on the main properties and qual[ity]"; SIMPL-31141/AC1, SIMPL-31767/AC1: "for each resource description in the list I receive the main properties".
findings.question: Are quality fields and sorting in the overview in scope for these stories?

findings.finding: The detail must include overall and per-dimension quality, but the detail operation returns only the credential, and quality sits in a separate QAR operation that answers 204 when there is no record. No criterion says what to show when a description has no QAR.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31143/AC1, SIMPL-31769/AC1: "the metadata quality score and quality classification for each dimension is returned"; catalogue-client-be GET /selfDescriptions/{selfDescriptionId} 200: VerifiableCredential, no quality fields; catalogue-be GET /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId}/qualityAssessmentRecord: 204.
findings.question: Which operation returns the quality block for the detail, and what is shown for a description without a QAR?

findings.finding: The own-catalogue detail stories have only the happy path. The federated twins (SIMPL-31148, SIMPL-31770) define not-found, failure and invalid-request cases; here a builder must guess them.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31143/AC1 and SIMPL-31769/AC1 are the only criteria; catalogue-client-be GET /selfDescriptions/{selfDescriptionId} defines 400, 401, 404, 500.
findings.question: Do the error criteria of SIMPL-31148 and SIMPL-31770 also apply to own-catalogue details?

findings.finding: This own-catalogue API story is said to be covered by SIMPL-33885 and SIMPL-31150, which are both about federated details. The coverage link looks misplaced.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31769 note: "covered with the implementation of SIMPL-33885 together with SIMPL-31150"; SIMPL-33885 title: "API to get detail of federated resource description".
findings.question: Which story or ticket builds the own-catalogue detail API?

findings.finding: Three stories require the schema to come back with a federated detail, while the Trustor and Trusted stories have the schema struck and the adapter contract says it returns no separate schema. The UI cannot render the detail without knowing where the schema comes from.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31148/AC1: "the Governance Authority successfully returns the Resource Description details and the associated schema"; SIMPL-31770/AC1: "the applicable schema ... is included in the returned result"; SIMPL-33885/AC1: "return the Resource Description details together with the related schema"; SIMPL-31153/AC2: "-along with the associated schema-"; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /federated/resourceDescriptions/{id}: "does not return a separate schema".
findings.question: Is the schema part of the federated detail response, and if not, where does the UI get the Trustor's schema?
options: schema returned with the detail (contract and SIMPL-31150/31153 to change)
no schema; UI uses a generic or SEARCH schema (SIMPL-31148/31770/33885 to change)

findings.finding: Failures map to an "appropriate" message; not-found and access-denied are not separated from a backend failure. A single generic message is a fair default.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31148/AC2: "the UI displays an appropriate error message"; SIMPL-31148/AC3: "an appropriate validation error message".
findings.question: Is one generic message enough, or do not-found and access-denied need their own texts?

findings.finding: Downstream failures must return "the corresponding error response according to the defined API contract", but the contract of the detail operation has only 400, 401, 404 and 500. The technical description asks for forbidden and timeout responses that the contract does not have, and SIMPL-33885/AC4 says 500 for unexpected errors.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31770/AC4: "the API returns the corresponding error response according to the defined API contract"; SIMPL-31770 technical description: "return defined not-found, forbidden, timeout, and downstream-error responses"; SIMPL-33885/AC4: "HTTP 500 Internal Server Error"; catalogue-client-be GET /selfDescriptions/{selfDescriptionId}: 400, 401, 404, 500.
findings.question: Which statuses apply to policy-denied, Trustor timeout and Trustor unreachable (403, 504, 502, or 500 for all)?

findings.finding: SIMPL-33885 adds a "dataspace/catalogue identifier" (one value or two?), while SIMPL-31770 says the API accepts "the resource identifier returned by the federated search" and keeps the own-catalogue path unchanged. The contract makes catalogueId required for every call, own catalogue included.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-33885/AC1: "a valid dataspace/catalogue identifier"; SIMPL-31770 technical description: "accept the resource identifier returned by the federated search ... keep the own-catalogue lookup behavior unchanged"; catalogue-client-be GET /selfDescriptions/{selfDescriptionId}: catalogueId required: true.
findings.question: Is the identifier a single catalogueId, and is it required for own-catalogue detail requests too?

findings.finding: The ids jump from AC1 to AC4; AC2 and AC3 do not exist. Harmless for the build, but tickets may refer to missing ids.
findings.question: Confirm that AC2 and AC3 were removed on purpose.

findings.finding: "Refuses the request" names no status. The adapter contract says gateway authentication and policy errors are outside it, and the technical description says the resource must not be exposed when it does not exist. A tester cannot tell 401, 403 or 404.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31150/AC2, AC3: "Simpl-Open refuses the request and does not return the protected resource description"; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /federated/resourceDescriptions/{id}: "Gateway-generated authentication and ABAC errors are outside this adapter response contract", responses 200, 400, 404, 406, 500.
findings.question: Which status does the Trusted GA receive for an untrusted caller, missing attributes and a policy denial; is a denial disguised as 404?
options: 404 for all, to hide existence

findings.finding: The story's technical description puts authentication, attribute mapping and policy evaluation in the adapter operation, but the adapter contract says the gateway does these and the adapter does not repeat them. Which component a test targets depends on the answer.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31150 technical description: "The operation must: authenticate the calling Trusted Governance Authority ... invoke the R24 identity-attribute mapping"; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /federated/resourceDescriptions/{id}: "The gateway authenticates ... maps the Consumer's identity attributes, and evaluates discovery ABAC ... The adapter does not repeat gateway authorization".
findings.question: Is mapping and policy evaluation built in the adapter or in the gateway?
options: gateway (adapter only receives User-Attributes)
adapter

findings.finding: The technical description lists not-found, mapping-unavailable and downstream-error cases and test cases for them, but no criterion states their outcome. The contract has a 404.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31150 technical description: "must not expose the resource description when the resource does not exist ... the identity mapping is unavailable"; "Add positive, not-found, unauthorised, missing-attributes, policy-denied, federation-revoked-after-discovery, and downstream-error test cases".
findings.question: What does the Trustor return for not-found, mapping unavailable and catalogue unavailable?

findings.finding: The Trusted-side operations (xfsc-advsearch-be to the Trusted adapter, and Trusted adapter to Trustor adapter) are required by the story but are in no entry file; the only federated detail operation is the Trustor-side one. "I forward the request" has no observable contract.

findings.finding: The named operation catalogue-be POST /schemas takes a raw RDF or SHACL file, has no schemaType, name, title or resourceType field, requires no role ("N/A"), and has no 409 response. None of the three criteria can be met through this operation as defined.

another component's schema API

findings.finding: The uniqueness rule differs: SIMPL-31815 rejects a second SEARCH schema only when another is published, SIMPL-31816 when one "already exists", and the technical notes say "only one". The hints add open questions on revoked schemas and name reuse.

form-based schema editor

findings.finding: The main business object has two live names. The stories, the business process and all three CDMs say resource description (CDM class ResourceDescription). The catalogue-be API says SelfDescription in every schema and path, the adapter uses both (/selfDescriptions for search, /resourceDescriptions for participant and federated detail), and catalogue-client-be uses selfDescriptions. The federated operations still to be defined (F-022, F-052) force a builder to pick one.
findings.evidence: BP05B and BP06 titles and steps: "resource description"; CDM:catalogue-be:ResourceDescription; catalogue-be common-components.yaml schemas SelfDescription, SelfDescriptions, SelfDescriptionResult, SelfDescriptionStatus; catalogue-be paths /self-descriptions and /selfDescriptions/quickSearch; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /selfDescriptions and GET /participants/resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId}, GET /federated/resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId}; catalogue-client-be GET /selfDescriptions/{selfDescriptionId}. The catalogue-client-be CDM already removed SelfDescription: "SelfDescription is not a concept of the Federated Catalogue CDM, which owns the resource description as ResourceDescription".
findings.question: Which name do new operations, schemas and events use, and is self-description kept only as a legacy wire name with a written mapping?
options: Resource description in all new contracts and texts; existing SelfDescription schemas and /selfDescriptions paths stay as documented legacy names, mapped in the glossary
Rename the existing schemas and paths to ResourceDescription (breaking change, versioned API)
Keep self-description on the wire everywhere and resource description in business texts, with the mapping written down

findings.finding: A resource description is identified under at least eight names, and it is not stated which of them name the same value. The search result items carry only claimsGraphUri, the detail call takes selfDescriptionId, the adapter takes resourceDescriptionId, and catalogue-be has both a per-record id and a resourceKey "stable across versions". A tester cannot pass the identifier from a search result to the detail call with confidence, and a builder cannot tell whether revoke and QAR act on one version or on the whole resource description.
findings.evidence: CDM:catalogue-be:ResourceDescription.resourceIdentifier; catalogue-be SelfDescription.id, .sdHash, .resourceKey ("Stable identifier for the resource across versions"), path selfDescriptionId, DELETE /self-descriptions/{self_description_hash}, GET /self-descriptions filters ids and hashes; query-mapper-adapter-be path resourceDescriptionId and GET .../version "list of resource descriptions with the same parent resource description id"; search items n.claimsGraphUri (catalogue-be, adapter) and i.claimsGraphUri (catalogue-client-be v1); catalogue-client-be selfDescriptionId example did:web:registry.gaia-x.eu:DataOffering:...; SIMPL-31150, SIMPL-31153, SIMPL-31770 technical descriptions: "resource identifier".
findings.question: Which identifier names a resource description across its versions, which names one version, and is the claimsGraphUri of a search result the selfDescriptionId and resourceDescriptionId of the detail calls?
options: resourceIdentifier (= resourceKey) for the resource description across versions, id for one version; search results expose resourceIdentifier; paths use {resourceDescriptionId}
One identifier only (the credential subject id, today claimsGraphUri); versions addressed by version number
Keep all names, and add a written mapping per API to the CDM identifier

findings.finding: The overall quality result has four names for the score and four for the classification. The criteria filter on overallCategory, which no API or CDM has. The Consumer-facing search (catalogue-client-be v1) returns qualityScore and qualityClassification, while catalogue-be and the adapter return overallScore and overallClassification. A test written from the criteria asserts on a field the response does not carry.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-29292/AC2, SIMPL-29293/AC2: "overallScore"; SIMPL-29292/AC3, SIMPL-29293/AC3: "overallCategory"; SIMPL-27998/AC1: "overall score"; SIMPL-31140 Scenario 4, SIMPL-31143/AC1, SIMPL-31769/AC1, BP6.7.3: "metadata quality score", "quality classification"; catalogue-be SearchResponsePayload n.overallScore, n.overallClassification and SelfDescriptionQualityOverallResult.score, .classification; query-mapper-adapter-be searchResponsePayload n.overallScore, n.overallClassification; catalogue-client-be v1 GET /selfDescriptions example i.qualityScore, i.qualityClassification; CDM:query-mapper-adapter-be:QualityAssessmentRecord.qualityScore and data-quality-rules.md QualityAssessmentRecord.qualityScore, qualityClassification, OverallQualityRating.weightedScore; catalogue-client-be.md: "SelfDescriptionScore".
findings.question: Which field names does a search result and a detail carry for the overall score and classification, and is overallCategory meant as overallClassification?
options: Business terms overall quality score and overall quality classification; wire names overallScore and overallClassification in every API; CDM attributes renamed to match
Wire names qualityScore and qualityClassification as in the CDM and the Consumer-facing API; catalogue-be and adapter renamed
Keep both, with a written mapping per API, and correct the criteria to the Consumer-facing names

findings.finding: "Federated catalogue" names two different things. In the stories and the business process it is a catalogue of another (Trustor) data space. In the CDMs and API texts the Federated Catalogue is the catalogue-be service of the own data space, and the adapter's local search says it searches "the Federated Catalogue". A builder of the federated search can read a requirement on federated catalogues as one on the own catalogue service.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31102/AC2: "the list of federated catalogues"; SIMPL-31768: "only from the catalogues of federated data spaces"; BP06 search scopes: "Federated catalogue search: search across multiple data spaces"; CDM:query-mapper-adapter-be:FederatedCatalogue ("stores ResourceDescriptions and evaluates catalogue search requests"), CDM:catalogue-client-be:FederatedCatalogue, schema-manager-be.md FederatedCatalogue; catalogue-be.md purpose: "Federated Catalogue Service (simpl-fc-service)"; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /selfDescriptions (local): "Search the Federated Catalogue for Resource descriptions"; federatedResourceDescriptionPayload: "Complete Federated Catalogue resource description"; catalogue-client-be v1 q: "filter self-descriptions in the federated catalog".
findings.question: Which name does the catalogue-be service carry in business texts and CDMs, so that federated catalogue only means a catalogue of a Trustor data space?
options: Federated catalogue only for a Trustor data space's catalogue (as BP06); the service becomes catalogue service (catalogue-be) in CDMs and API texts
Keep Federated Catalogue for the service, and say catalogue of a federated data space (or Trustor catalogue) in stories and APIs
Define both meanings in the glossary and qualify each use

findings.finding: The lifecycle of a resource description is not defined once. The CDM and API know active and revoked; the criteria and the process speak of submitted, valid, published, not published and stored. The process revokes the previous version when a new one is published, but no transition or state covers that. The publish operation can answer 202 "accepted but the validation is not finished yet", a pending state that no value set has. DELETE removes a description "entirely", a step the process does not have.
findings.evidence: CDM:catalogue-be:ResourceDescription.lifecycleStatus: active, revoked; catalogue-be SelfDescriptionStatus enum active, revoked; SIMPL-27998/AC1 to AC3: "published in the catalogue", "not stored"; BP05B.07 "published", BP05B.11 and BP5B.5.10 "revokes the current (previous) resource description version"; catalogue-be POST /self-descriptions 202: "The request was accepted but the validation is not finished yet"; DELETE /self-descriptions/{self_description_hash}; catalogue-be.md: "Deletion removes it entirely from the catalogue"; query-mapper-adapter-be PATCH /participants/resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId}: revoke, idempotent.
findings.question: Is published the business label of active, is there a pending state after submission, does a superseded version become revoked or a separate state, and is deletion part of the lifecycle?
options: States published (stored value active) and revoked; superseded versions become revoked; no pending state (202 removed); delete is an administrative purge outside the lifecycle
Add states pending and superseded to the CDM value set and the API enum, with the transitions listed next to the CDM
Keep active and revoked as written and change the criteria to say active

findings.finding: "Active" carries three meanings: a lifecycle value of a resource description, the Metadata Quality Profile resolved for the latest published schema version (whose own lifecycle has no active value), and a catalogue's federation flag. The trust relation behind that flag is also called trusted, no longer trusted, federation enabled and authenticated.
findings.evidence: catalogue-be SelfDescriptionStatus active; catalogue-client-be GET /schemas/{schemaName}/qualityProfiles/active: "active Metadata Quality Profile resolved for the latest published schema version"; schema-manager-be.md MetadataQualityProfile.lifecycleStatus: PUBLISHED, REVOKED; catalogue-client-be v1 CatalogueInfo.active and catalogue-client-be.md Catalogue: "whether its federation status is active"; SIMPL-31113/AC2 "no longer consider trusted GA as trusted"; SIMPL-31150/AC1 "its federation with this Governance Authority is still enabled"; SIMPL-31150/AC2 "unauthenticated or no-longer-trusted".
findings.question: Which word names each of the three concepts, and what are the values of the federation (trust) status?
options: Resource description: published; profile: applicable (or active) Metadata Quality Profile, defined in the glossary; catalogue: federation enabled / disabled
Keep active for all three and define each use in the glossary

findings.finding: The parts of a Quality Assessment Record have three sets of names. The owning CDM (Quality Scoring Service) has OverallQualityRating, DimensionRating and RuleOutcome. The catalogue-be API redefines them as SelfDescriptionQualityOverallResult, ...DimensionResult and ...RuleResult with other attribute names, and the Consumer-facing record uses SelfDescriptionScore, DimensionScore and RuleEvaluation. The record is also exposed twice: as an opaque JSON-LD graph and as a structured qualityAssessment in the publication response. The threshold source is called metadata quality definition, Metadata Quality Profile and Minimum Quality Profile.
findings.evidence: data-quality-rules.md: OverallQualityRating.weightedScore, thresholdStatus; DimensionRating.score, dimensionWeight, thresholdStatus; RuleOutcome.outcome, ruleType; catalogue-be SelfDescriptionQualityAssessment {rules, dimensions, overall}, SelfDescriptionQualityRuleResult {id, name, status}, SelfDescriptionQualityStatus PASSED, FAILED; catalogue-be QualityAssessmentRecord {@context, @graph}; SelfDescriptionPublicationResponse.qualityAssessment; catalogue-client-be.md: "SelfDescriptionScore, DimensionScore and RuleEvaluation of the response are OverallQualityRating, DimensionRating and RuleOutcome"; SIMPL-27998/AC1 "metadata quality definition", AC2 "metadata quality definition (MQP)"; SIMPL-29292/AC3 "Metadata Quality Profile (MQP)"; catalogue-client-be v1 GET /selfDescriptions: "active Minimum Quality Profile (MQP)".
findings.question: Does the catalogue API use the owner's names for the record's parts, and which representation is the Quality Assessment Record the catalogue stores and returns?
options: Use the Quality Scoring Service names (OverallQualityRating, DimensionRating, RuleOutcome and their attributes) in every API; the JSON-LD graph is the record, the structured form is a documented projection
Keep the catalogue-be names as the catalogue's own read model, marked as a projection of the external record in the CDM

findings.finding: Resource type and offering type look like one concept with two names and four spellings: lower case (data, application, infrastructure), upper case (DATA, APPLICATION), short forms (App, Infra, Data) and PascalCase shape names (Application, DataOffering). The schema stories reject a SEARCH schema when a resourceType is given, so the accepted values matter for the 400 tests.

findings.question: Are resource type and offering type the same concept, and which values and spelling do the API, the CDM and the criteria use?
options: One concept, resource type, with the closed set data, application, infrastructure in lower case; offeringType kept as the shape's property name and mapped
Two concepts: offering type (closed set on the description) and resource type (open, PascalCase, on the schema), each defined in the glossary

findings.finding: "Schema" names different things in one component. catalogue-be's /schemas operations manage the original catalogue store of ontologies, shapes and vocabularies (OntologySchema, latest composite schema), while its CDM says schema management is external and those legacy endpoints are excluded. The Schema Manager schema has a schemaName, a schemaType and versions. The schema is identified as schemaId, schemaName, name or uri depending on the API. The stories send schema creation to "POST /schemas", which in catalogue-be is the legacy store.
findings.evidence: catalogue-be t1 GET/POST /schemas, GET/PUT/DELETE /schemas/{schemaId}, GET /schemas/latest; OntologySchema {ontologies, shapes, vocabularies}; catalogue-be.md assumption: "it excludes legacy schema-management and session-management endpoints"; schema-manager-be.md Schema.schemaName, schemaType RESOURCE, SEARCH; catalogue-client-be v2 GET /schemas/{schemaId}/content and GET /schemas/{schemaName}/qualityProfiles/active, list example {name: health, schemaId: applicationHealth}; catalogue-be POST /schemas/{schemaName}/recalcQualityScore; EventDataSchema.name, .uri; SIMPL-31815/AC1: "the endpoint POST /schemas with schemaType=\"SEARCH\"".
findings.question: Which schema concept do catalogue-be's /schemas operations expose, are they still in scope, and which identifier names a schema?
options: The catalogue references the Schema Manager schema only, identified by schemaName; catalogue-be's legacy /schemas operations are removed from the contract
Keep the legacy store under another name (for example ontology store) and reserve schema for the Schema Manager concept

findings.finding: Identity attributes, their federation mapping and discovery access policies carry the federated search criteria, but no CDM in the input set models them, as owned or as external. The only related class, AccessPolicyFilter, is owned by the Query Mapper, is "interaction only", and never appears in the stories. The same ideas have many names: identity attributes, public identity attributes, Consumer's attributes, mapped attributes, User-Attributes; discovery access policies, access policy values, discovery ABAC.

findings.question: Which context owns identity attributes, the attribute mapping and the discovery access policy, and which external classes do the catalogue CDMs add for them?
options: Identity attributes and attribute mapping external (IAA / authentication provider); discovery access policy part of the resource description (owned by the catalogue); AccessPolicyFilter renamed or explained in those terms
Keep them out of the catalogue CDMs and state in the CDM that the gateway owns all of it, removing the policy steps from the catalogue criteria

findings.finding: The search result item is an anonymous node (n in catalogue-be and the adapter, i in catalogue-client-be v1) that holds the general service properties summary, the quality summary and claimsGraphUri. No CDM class names it. Its fields (name, description, inLanguage) differ from the catalogue-be CDM attributes (serviceName, serviceDescription, serviceLanguage), and the referencing CDM lists yet other ones. The stories call the same content "the main properties" without listing them.

options: Main properties = GeneralServiceProperties summary; CDM attributes renamed to the shape names (name, description, inLanguage, offeringType, serviceAccessPoint); the result item gets a named schema (for example ResourceDescriptionSummary)
Keep the CDM names and document the mapping to the shape names

findings.finding: Each API has a CDM, but the alignment tables no longer match the entry files. The catalogue-be CDM says legacy schema and session endpoints are excluded, yet the tier 1 entry file has them, and the generic /query operation has no concept at all. The Query Mapper CDM lists neither the Governance Authority search operations nor the federated detail operation, and its scope does not mention federation. The catalogue-client-be CDM lists /governanceAuthority operations that its v1 file does not have, and places the detail operation with catalogueId in v1 while it is in the v2 entry file.

options: Update the three CDMs: add the federated operations and their concepts; remove session, query and legacy schema operations from the catalogue-be contract
Keep the operations and add their concepts to the CDMs

findings.finding: RecalcQualityScoreJob is modelled as an owned business record, but the API only returns a 202 acknowledgement without an id that can be read again. The CDM also contradicts itself on the trigger: one note says the schema-events webhook "is not the trigger for recalculation", the endpoint table says a SchemaPublished or SchemaRevoked event "triggers recalculation". findings.finding: It is not defined how the Consumer's identity attributes reach the services that apply the discovery access policy. Local tier 2 searches (catalogue-be quickSearch and advancedSearch, adapter GET /selfDescriptions and POST /selfDescriptions/advancedSearch) take User-Attributes as an optional header. D20 and E1 say tier 2 services read User-Attributes and that no gateway is built, so tests send the gateway headers. In an end-to-end search the call comes from catalogue-client-be or the Trusted adapter, not from a test, and the Tier 1 operations have no User-Attributes header. Nothing says which service turns the Consumer's JWT into User-Attributes, from which claim, and D30 has the Trusted adapter send User-Attributes to the Trustor without saying where it gets them. D20 defines 400 for a missing header only on Trustor operations; on local operations one builder returns 400, another treats it as no attributes (D21: only descriptions with an empty list), a third skips filtering.

findings.finding: The publication operation, the main path of the quality gate, has no request contract. The body is 'type: string' with no example. The description says validation covers 'schema version, resource version number, and provider ownership' and rejects a conflicting version (409), but no field is named. A builder needs to know where the schema reference sits (D17 takes the threshold from that schema's active profile), how a new version names its resource description and carries its version number (D18 revokes the previous version, D7 addresses versions by number), and how ownership is checked (against which header or claim). The 201 response returns SelfDescription without the quality assessment, while SelfDescriptionPublicationResponse with qualityAssessment hangs on POST /self-descriptions, which D4 does not build; D11 refers to 'the publication response'. Two builders will accept different payloads and return different 201 bodies, and a tester cannot write a valid fixture.

findings.question: What is the publication request (credential fields for schema name and version, resource description id and version number, provider identity), which checks give 400, 403, 409 and 422, and which schema does the 201 body use?
options: Body is the signed credential; schema from credentialSubject dct:conformsTo (dct:schemaName, dct:hasVersion), version from currentVersion in a named property, ownership from providedBy against User-Attributes; 201 returns SelfDescriptionPublicationResponse
Same body, 201 returns SelfDescription only and the quality is read through the QAR operation
Add an explicit JSON envelope {schemaName, schemaVersion, version, credential}

findings.finding: The security schemes do not describe the decided authentication and roles. catalogue-be uses OAuth2Auth at root but defines only 'jwt' (http bearer), so the reference is broken in both entry files and in the root spec. The adapter defines an oauth2 authorizationCode flow with placeholder URLs (auth.example.com) and scopes read and write, not Keycloak and not roles. catalogue-client-be uses a plain bearer JWT 'IAA cloud gateway'. The role CATALOGUE_SEARCHER of D20 and E1 appears only in descriptions of catalogue-be tier 2 operations, not on any Tier 1 operation. D20 gives Tier 1 401 for no token and 403 without the role, but the adapter Tier 1 searches list neither 401 nor 403 and catalogue-client-be lists no 403 anywhere. catalogue-be tier 2 operations also declare Authorization as a header parameter, which OpenAPI ignores when a security scheme applies.

findings.finding: catalogue-be returns two error formats. The shared responses ClientError, NotFound, Unauthorized, Forbidden, ServerError, Conflict and Unprocessible are application/json with Error {code, message}; the QAR, quick and advanced search, recalculation and webhook errors are application/problem+json Problem. A client of the built operations has to parse both (for example quickSearch 400 is Problem, 500 is Error). D17 builds on Error.code (QUALITY_THRESHOLD_NOT_MET, QUALITY_ASSESSMENT_FAILED). 21a did not report API-45 for these responses. catalogue-client-be v2 defines five copies of the problem schema with a property literally named additionalProperties.

findings.finding: Informing Consumers about a new version or a revocation is a main step of BP05B, but its party, its trigger and its receiver are all open. The step texts are passive ('the Consumers of this resource are informed'). The requirement titles 5B.6 and 5B.9 make the Provider the sender, while the 5B.8 description makes the Governance Authority the sender. No decision says which service learns of the change and how: D18 and D35 define publication of a new version and revocation as synchronous calls that emit nothing, and no event, webhook or callback exists for either change. The catalogue also does not know who the 'Consumers of this resource' are: they are the parties with usage contracts (BP07), which live outside the catalogue. Two builders would build different flows: one emits an event from catalogue-be, the other builds nothing.
findings.evidence: BP05B.12 'If a resource description is updated, the Consumers of this resource are informed about the new version'; BP05B.15 same for revocation; 5B.6 title 'A Provider notifies Consumers', description 'enabling a Provider to automatically notify Consumers'; 5B.8 description 'Simpl-Open shall enable the Governance Authority to ... Notify Consumers regarding the revocation'; 5B.9 'support a Provider to automatically notify Consumers'. D18 transitions and D35 201 outcome name no event; D4 builds no notification operation; BA-025 and BA-028 (no criterion).
findings.question: Which party informs the Consumers (Provider, Governance Authority, or the catalogue service on their behalf), what signal starts it (an event from catalogue-be on publication of a new version and on revocation, or an action in another component), and who resolves the list of Consumers with a contract? Or are both notification steps out of the catalogue build, to be recorded as a decision?
options: Out of the catalogue build: record a step 30 addendum that BP05B.12 and BP05B.15 belong to the contract or connector side, with no event from catalogue-be
catalogue-be publishes an event (resource description superseded, resource description revoked) after the state change and does not wait; another component resolves Consumers and informs them
The Provider informs Consumers itself through its own connector after a successful revoke or publication response

findings.finding: The process gives a superseded version and a revoked resource description two different follow-ups (BP05B.12 inform about new version, BP05B.15 inform about revocation), but the decided lifecycle has one state for both: revoked. Neither the stored record nor the version list says why a version was revoked. Any later notification (B-001) or the Provider's version history (5B.1.3) cannot tell 'replaced by version n+1' from 'withdrawn by the Provider'. The 409 rule of D35 works only because the latest version is revoked solely by an explicit revoke, which is an implicit rule, not a stored fact.
findings.evidence: D18 'Publishing a new version revokes the previous published version'; decided glossary: revoked = 'State of a withdrawn or superseded resource description'; D40 version items carry status active or revoked only; D35 '409 conflict' when 'the latest version of that id is revoked (the Provider revoked the resource description)'; D-005 asked whether a superseded version is a separate state.
findings.question: Does a superseded version need to be told apart from a withdrawn one (a separate state such as superseded, or a revocation reason on the version), so that BP05B.12 and BP05B.15 and the version history can be driven from the record?
options: Keep one revoked state and add a revocation reason (superseded or withdrawn) to the version metadata
Add a state superseded to the lifecycle
Keep D18 as is; nothing downstream needs the difference

findings.finding: The process makes revocation a hand-over between two parties: the Provider requests (BP05B.13), then the Governance Authority revokes 'upon receiving a request' (BP05B.14). The decisions collapse this into one synchronous Provider call with immediate effect: POST .../revoke with a publisher role and ownership check. That is a valid reading if the catalogue service acts for the Governance Authority automatically, but it is not stated, and there is no path for a Governance Authority to refuse a request or to revoke on its own initiative (for example a non-compliant description). D37 gives the Governance Authority no role on revoke at all.
findings.evidence: BP05B.13 'The Provider ... initiates the revocation'; BP05B.14 'Upon receiving a request for revocation, the Governance Authority revokes'; 5B.7 'request to the Governance Authority the revocation'; D18 'Revoke moves published to revoked'; D37 revoke needs a publisher role and simpl:providedBy equal to participant_id; BA-026, BA-027; P-012 (no story for revoke).
findings.question: Is the Governance Authority's revocation the automatic execution of a valid Provider request by the catalogue service (no review), and can the Governance Authority also revoke a resource description without a Provider request?
options: Automatic: the catalogue service revokes for the Governance Authority on a valid owner request; no Governance Authority initiative in this release
Automatic for owner requests, plus a Governance Authority revoke with its own role
A request state with Governance Authority approval before revocation

findings.finding: The two BP05B files give a different order for the main path. The process steps validate first and publish after (BP05B.05 validate, BP05B.06 remediate, BP05B.07 publish), which matches the decided synchronous gate (D17, D18: 201 or an error, no pending state). The dynamic view signs and 'publishes the signed self-description to the Catalogue' first, and only 'after publication' runs semantic validation and the quality check, then stores the description and notifies the end user. A builder who follows the dynamic view builds an asynchronous flow with a submitted or pending state that D18 rejects.
findings.evidence: bp05b-dynamic-view steps 5 to 8: 'Signing and Publication ... then publishes the signed self-description to the Catalogue'; 'Semantic Validation: After publication, the Catalogue ... initiates Semantic Validation'; 'the End User receives a confirmation notification'; 'Database Storage: Upon passing all validations'. README BP05B.05 to BP05B.07. D17 synchronous; D18 'no pending state, so the 202 response is not used'.
findings.question: Can the dynamic view be aligned with the process steps (validation and the quality gate before publication, one synchronous answer), and the word 'publishes' in step 5 changed to 'submits'?
options: Align the dynamic view with BP05B.05 to BP05B.07 and D17, D18
Keep an asynchronous flow and add a pending state to the lifecycle (reopens D18)

findings.target: BP05B.04 to BP05B.07, bp05b-dynamic-view steps 4 and 5
findings.finding: Publication spans several components before the catalogue answers: the dynamic view registers the description as an asset in the Connector (step 4), signs it with the Signer and stores a signed copy in the Provider's Wallet (step 5), and only then submits it to the catalogue. The catalogue can still refuse it (400, 403, 409, 422, 500 under D35 and D17). Nothing says what happens to the connector asset and the wallet copy of a refused description: undone, kept as a draft, or reused on the resubmission that BP05B.06 asks for. A refusal can leave an offer registered in the connector for a description that is in no catalogue, and a resubmission can register a second asset.
findings.evidence: bp05b-dynamic-view step 4 'the self-description is directed to the Connector component, where it is registered as an asset'; step 5 'A copy of the signed self-description is also stored locally in the Provider's Wallet'; BP05B.06 'The Provider must remediate and resubmit'; D35 check order and D17 outcomes define the catalogue side only ('not stored').
findings.question: When the catalogue refuses a submission, what happens to the connector asset and the wallet copy made before it, and does a resubmission reuse them? Is registering the asset after a successful publication an option?
options: Register the connector asset only after the catalogue returns 201
Keep the asset and the copy as drafts; resubmission reuses them; define a cleanup for abandoned drafts
Undo both (compensating steps) on any refusal

findings.finding: Semantic validation of a submitted description against its schema and the vocabulary is a named main-path check (BP05B.05) and the dynamic view gives it to the catalogue, but no criterion and no decision defines it. D35 checks the JSON shape, four required fields, that the schema version is published, ownership and the revoked state; D17 adds the quality gate. Whether the credential subject is validated against the SHACL shapes of the schema version, and what a violation returns, is open. One builder will reject a description that breaks its shapes, another will publish it.
findings.evidence: BP05B.05 'performs syntactic validation, semantic validation against schema and vocabulary, and quality-rules validation'; 5B.5.7 'Validates semantics', 5B.5.8 'Notifies about semantic errors'; dynamic view step 6 'the Catalogue on the governance node initiates Semantic Validation'; D35 list of checks; D17 quality gate. BA-022, BA-023.
findings.question: Does catalogue-be validate the credential subject against the SHACL shapes of the referenced schema version before the quality gate, and does a violation return 400 invalidInput with the failing shape in detail? Or is semantic validation part of the Quality Scoring Service call?
options: catalogue-be validates against the schema shapes; violation gives 400 invalidInput, nothing stored, before the quality gate
The Quality Scoring Service covers it; a violation is a quality failure (422)
Out of this build; record a decision

findings.finding: The process assumes a new description or version 'always uses the latest version of a schema', and 5B.5.2 has the Governance Authority notify the Provider about an inactive schema. D35 accepts any schema name and version that is 'a published RESOURCE schema version'. It is not said whether an older version stays published after a newer one is published, so a submission against an older version is accepted by one builder and refused by another, and the refusal for an inactive schema has no own outcome.
findings.evidence: BP05B assumption 1; 5B.2 'based on the latest versions of the resource description schema'; 5B.3 'based on the latest version of the schema'; 5B.5.2 'Alerts providers to schema status issues'; D35 'schema name and version not a published RESOURCE schema version in the Schema Manager 400 invalidInput'; D41 GET /schemas returns 'the latest published' version. BA-016, BA-017.
findings.question: Must the submitted dct:hasVersion be the latest published version of the schema, and does a submission against an older or revoked version get its own 400 detail?
options: Latest version only: older version gives 400 invalidInput with a detail naming the latest version
Any published version is accepted; the assumption is relaxed

findings.finding: BP06.04 is titled 'Conduct a quality rating of the resources' but its text describes the Consumer accessing the returned results per scope. It sits before the federated steps BP06.05 to BP06.10 and the collection step BP06.11, so read in order the Consumer sees results before the Trustor results are collected. The decided flow returns one grouped response after all groups are done (D24, D25), and no quality rating happens at search time: the score comes from the record stored at publication (D17, D26). The title and the position of BP06.04 disagree with the decided flow.
findings.evidence: BP06.04 title vs text 'The Consumer accesses the resource descriptions returned for the search ... The search results are available to the Consumer'; BP06.11 'These resource descriptions are provided together to the Consumer'; D24 one grouped response; D17 QAR stored at publication; D26 Trustor items carry null quality.
findings.question: Can BP06.04 be renamed (for example 'Consult the search results') and moved after BP06.11, and is any quality rating done at search time, or only the stored rating applied as a filter?
options: Rename and move BP06.04 after BP06.11; quality is only read from the stored record
Keep the order and state that BP06.04 is the own-only path that skips BP06.05 to BP06.11

findings.finding: The failure of a Trustor in a federated search is defined (D25: group status unavailable, still 200), but the failure of the own catalogue is not. In a mixed search, the Trusted adapter searches its own catalogue-be as one group: if that call fails or times out, it is open whether the own group gets status unavailable or the whole search fails. In an own-only search (D33 routing to the local tier 2 operations), the status list names 400, 401 and 403 but no outcome for a failing catalogue-be. The UI texts of D23, D29 and D31 cover no search failure.
findings.evidence: D25 'A failing Trustor never fails the whole search' (Trustor only); D24 own catalogue is one group in the grouped response; D33 'Statuses: 401 and 403 as in D20 and D37; 400 invalidInput ...' with no 500; D36 500 problem type exists but no search case uses it.
findings.question: When the own catalogue fails during a search, does its group get status unavailable (mixed search) and does an own-only search return 500 internalServerError, and what text does the UI show?
options: Same rule as D25 for the own group in a mixed search; own-only search returns 500 and the UI shows 'The search could not be completed.'
Any own-catalogue failure fails the whole search with 500

findings.finding: A federated search creates load at every selected Trustor Governance Authority, another party, on behalf of one Consumer. The decided limits are a page size cap of 100 (D33) and a 10 second timeout (D25). There is no limit on the number of catalogueIds in one request, no rate limit per Consumer at the Trusted side, and no limit at the Trustor per Trusted Governance Authority. An automated Consumer can fan out many searches per second to all Trustors. No criterion or decision covers this abuse case.
findings.evidence: BP06.05 'forwards the search request to each Trustor Governance Authority'; D33 'catalogueIds required, at least one item' (no maximum), 'pageSize ... capped at 100'; D25 10 second timeout; D28 Trustor operations take no token in the build (D37); OWT-A06 asks abuse cases next to normal cases.
findings.question: Which limits apply to federated search: a maximum number of catalogueIds per request, a rate limit per Consumer at the Trusted side, a rate limit per Trusted Governance Authority at the Trustor (and its status, 429)? Which of these belong to the gateway?
options: maxItems on catalogueIds equal to the number of listed catalogues, plus 429 rate limits at the gateway on both sides, recorded as a decision
Gateway rate limits only, outside the catalogue build, recorded as a decision

findings.finding: The process has the Provider sign the description with its credentials (BP05B.04), but no step verifies the signature: BP05B.05 lists syntactic, semantic and quality validation only, and D35 says the build does not verify the proof. Ownership is checked against the token (D35), which limits the risk. The process should say which party verifies the signature and when.
findings.evidence: BP05B.04 'signs the new resource description with the Provider's credentials'; BP05B.05 list of validations; D35 'The build does not verify the proof' and owner question 'that the proof is verified elsewhere'. BA-015.
findings.question: Which party verifies the Provider's signature on a submitted description, and should BP05B.05 name that check?
options: catalogue-be verifies the proof before the other checks (400 on failure)
The gateway or the signer side verifies; BP05B.05 says so

findings.finding: Publishing a new version stores the new version and revokes the previous one (BP05B.07, BP05B.11, D18). D35 defines that a refused publication leaves the previous version published, but not that the two writes of a successful one are one transaction. If the revoke of the previous version fails after the new one is stored, two published versions exist, which D7 (detail returns the latest published version) does not expect.
findings.evidence: BP05B.11 'If the new version of the resource description is valid, the Governance Authority revokes the current (previous) resource description version'; D18; D35 'A failed publication of a new version leaves the previous version published'; D7.
findings.question: Confirm that storing the new version and revoking the previous one happen in one transaction in catalogue-be, so at most one published version exists per resource description.
options: One transaction; at most one published version per id is an invariant tests can check

findings.finding: The Provider consults its own descriptions (5B.1) through the same reads as a Consumer: the detail returns published versions only and both detail and version list apply the discovery access policy (D40, D34). A Provider whose identity attributes do not meet its own policy gets 404 on its own description, and a Provider cannot read the content of its own revoked description. The overview of own descriptions (5B.1.1) is out of the build by D4 (GET /self-descriptions not built).
findings.evidence: 5B.1.2 'consults the details of one of its own resource descriptions'; 5B.1.3 version history; D40 detail 'latest published version', versions 'applies the discovery access policy like the detail'; D31 404 when the policy is not met; D4 excludes GET /self-descriptions.
findings.question: Does the owner of a resource description bypass the discovery access policy on its own detail and version list, and may it read revoked versions?
options: Owner (simpl:providedBy equal to the caller) bypasses the policy; revoked versions readable by the owner only
No owner view in this build; 5B.1 out of scope by D4

findings.finding: Each submission calls the Quality Scoring Service synchronously (D17), and each new version revokes the previous one and, by the process, informs every Consumer of the resource (BP05B.12). The remediate-and-resubmit loop of BP05B.06 and repeated new versions have no limit, so an automated Provider can load the scoring service and flood Consumers with new-version notices. No abuse case is written down.
findings.evidence: BP05B.06 'The Provider must remediate and resubmit'; BP05B.08 new version; BP05B.12; D17 synchronous scoring call per submission; D35 no rate rule.
findings.question: Is a rate limit per Provider on POST /self-descriptions/resource needed (status 429), or is this left to the gateway?
options: Gateway rate limit, recorded as a decision
No limit in this release, accepted risk

findings.finding: The federated detail flow (the Trusted Governance Authority forwards a detail request, the Trustor maps attributes and returns the details) is a cross-party hand-over with four requirements (6.7.5 to 6.7.8), six stories and two decisions (D30, D31), but no process step. The process steps stop at the search; the Consumer opening a federated detail is only one sentence in BP06.04. The process text lags behind the stories.
findings.evidence: BP06.04 'can access and display the details of selected resource descriptions'; 6.7.5 to 6.7.8; SIMPL-31149 to SIMPL-31153, SIMPL-33885; D30, D31.
findings.question: Can BP06 add steps for the federated detail request (forward, map, provide, return), mirroring BP06.05 to BP06.10?
options: Add the detail steps to BP06
Keep them as requirements only

findings.finding: SIMPL-35874 (advanced search with the SEARCH schema for federated queries) has no link to the process, and BP06 has no text for it: BP06.01 and 6.1.2 speak of advanced search on 'attributes of the resource description' without saying that a federated advanced search uses the one federated search schema. The story belongs to BP06.01 and 6.1.2; the process text lags behind the story and D24, D29.
findings.evidence: BA-037; BP06 overview 'Advanced search: specify values for one or more attributes'; 6.1.2; D24 'In a mixed advanced search all catalogues ... are searched with the SEARCH schema fields'; D29.
findings.question: Can BP06.01 say that an advanced search over federated catalogues uses the federated search schema, and can SIMPL-35874 be linked to 6.1.2?
options: Add the sentence and the link

findings.finding: The DOME Marketplace scope (BP06.12, 6.8 to 6.10, prerequisite BP02G) has no story and no criterion, and 22a does not list it because the requirements have no detailed requirements. The step 30 glossary marks DOME offerings 'Out of the build (no story)' and cites D5, but D5's decision text is about searching all federated catalogues and does not mention DOME. The exclusion is therefore not in any decision text, and the failure and abuse cases of forwarding to DOME (an external party) stay unaddressed.
findings.evidence: BP06.12; 6.8 to 6.10 'None published at the time of capture'; decided glossary 'DOME Marketplace offering ... Out of the build (no story). D5'; D5 text; D23 selector lists only own and Trustor catalogues.
findings.question: Can the DOME exclusion be stated in a decision text (D5 or a new one), so the selector, the grouped response and the tests are known to have no DOME scope?
options: Extend D5 (or add a decision): DOME scope, BP06.12 and 6.8 to 6.10 out of this build
